name: Pale Teal
lede: Pale Teal is a washed-out, bluish green built by the modifier grammar "pale + [[teal]]", closest in our library to Celadon.

sections.title: A paler teal
sections.body:
Pale Teal comes from the xkcd 2010 color-name survey, where crowd respondents paired a shade word with a family name rather than coining something new [1]. The ISCC-NBS block for it reads "very light bluish green" [1]. In Munsell terms it sits near 9.1G 7.6/5.0, a light, moderately saturated green [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[light-sulphate-green]] and [[medium-aquamarine]], at The hex is a screen approximation; no pigment or dye is implied by the match [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Pale Teal is one of our rarer matches: it covers at least 2% of the canvas in 7 of 23,781 paintings, rarer than 82% of the named colors we track, close in family to [[aquamarine]], as photographed [2]. The within-painting lens, which asks where a color sits by lightness rather than by raw coverage, finds it in only 2 of those [2].

The earliest match is 1825 (nga-43713), with later ones running to 1940, 185 years before the name's own earliest record in 2010, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. A match this old says only that a similar-looking green was photographed there, not that the painter or anyone else used this name or mixed it the same way [2].
